bull_bear.body:
- In-house developed technologies for manufacturing various grades of polymer blends for different applications, with product quality stated to be on par with international standards (Annexure 'A', Technology Absorption — read in the strategy_outlook bundle)
- Ability to customise and promote new grades of polymer blends to meet specific domestic and international customer requirements
- Positioned as a supplier of a specialised, value-added intermediate to the fragmented non-tyre rubber segment, which accounts for over 50% of non-tyre rubber product output
- Debt-free balance sheet posture indicated by a nil Debt-Equity Ratio and nil Interest Coverage Ratio disclosed in the MD&A key-ratio table
- Product portfolio extended beyond polymer blends into complementary raw materials for international customers, broadening the global footprint
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Structural margin pressure from a highly competitive, price-sensitive rubber industry — MD&A states the industry operates in a highly competitive and price-sensitive environment because both the user base and the supply chain are fragmented, limiting the Company's ability to hold realisations.
- Raw-material and crude-linked input price volatility — MD&A notes volatility in raw material prices including petrochemical-linked inputs and natural rubber; pricing pressure is further influenced by these swings, and softening input prices depressed realisations and margins even while supporting demand.
- Realisation compression when input prices fall — Opportunities and Threats records that stability in supply caused a fall in prices which has put margins under pressure - a fall-through risk where lower input costs are passed to customers faster than they are recovered.
- Weakening global economic conditions and persistent inflation — The only risk management explicitly names in the MD&A Risks and Concerns section, flagged as a potential area of concern.
- Export-market demand weakness and geopolitical / trade disruption — The Directors' Report describes heightened geopolitical tensions, regional conflicts, tariff realignments and supply chain diversification creating uncertainty in global growth; the Company saw weaker demand in export markets during the year and had to lean on domestic sales to offset it.
- Single-segment concentration in Polymers and Polymer Compounds — MD&A states the primary segment the Company operates in is Polymers and Polymer Compounds and their related products, so there is no diversification cushion against a downturn in rubber compounding; the planned Plastics compounding line is the stated response.
- Earnings sensitivity to a quoted investment portfolio held outside the operating business — MD&A and the Directors' Report attribute the fall in other income and the reduction in Return on Networth to a sharp fall in the value of the investment portfolio and to fair valuation of quoted investments decreasing amid subdued financial markets - non-operating earnings that swing with equity markets.
- Very small operating scale and thin management bench — MD&A discloses the Company currently employs about 35 employees in all categories, a small base relative to the newly approved Plastics/Plastics compounding business line and Wadivare capacity expansion it must execute.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The Company manufactures polymer blends and polymer compounds through rubber compounding — a specialised, value-added process of formulating rubber mixtures with raw materials to achieve target processing characteristics and end-use performance. Its output is a critical intermediate input for MSMEs making diverse rubber products, and it also supplies complementary raw materials to customers in international markets. Its primary reported segment is Polymers and Polymer Compounds and their related products.

outlook.body:
- Establish a new business line in Plastics/Plastics compounding and expand capacity of the existing business at the Wadivare factory site, backed by a Board-approved estimated capex of Rs 35.00 crore
- Grow the domestic business, having mitigated weaker export-market demand through a stronger focus on domestic sales where volume growth remained encouraging
- Customise and promote new grades of polymer blends to meet the requirements of domestic and international markets
- Optimise product mix, enhance operational efficiencies and strengthen market presence while closely monitoring global developments
- Supply complementary raw materials alongside polymer blends to international customers to broaden the product portfolio and global footprint
- Continue strategic investment in Information Technology as a lever for business growth
- Continue in-house technology development for new grades of polymer blends, having brought final product quality on par with international standards (Annexure A, Technology Absorption)
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY 2025-26 the Board approved estimated capital expenditure of Rs 35.00 crore for the establishment of a new business line in Plastics/Plastics compounding and for capacity expansion of the existing business, both at the Wadivare factory site. No commissioning date, ramp-up schedule or capacity quantum for this project is disclosed in the annual-report text supplied. Separately, the Company installed and commissioned an 80 KW rooftop solar system at its Nashik (Satpur) plant on September 21, 2021 (Annexure 'A' to the Directors' Report, read in the strategy_outlook bundle); capital investment on energy conservation during FY 2025-26 was stated as NIL. Capital commitments as at March 31, 2026 were NIL (previous year NIL).
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Demand for the Company's products remained healthy during the year, particularly from domestic industrial segments such as automotive components, infrastructure-linked products and general engineering applications, which continue to drive rubber consumption
- The domestic rubber market was valued at approximately USD 3.3-4.2 billion in recent years and is expected to grow at a CAGR of around 5-7% over the medium term, driven by demand from automotive, infrastructure and industrial sectors
- The non-tyre segment, served largely by MSMEs, contributes over 50% of non-tyre rubber product output and is the Company's primary customer base
- Indian GDP growth estimated at approximately 6.5% in FY 2025-26, supported by strong domestic demand, sustained government capital expenditure and manufacturing momentum
- Volatility in raw material prices, including softening in petrochemical-linked inputs: while supportive of demand, it pressured realisations and margins across the polymer compounding value chain
- Stability in supply led to a fall in prices which has put margins under pressure
- The rubber industry operates in a highly competitive and price-sensitive environment due to the fragmented structure of both the user base and the supply chain, with pricing further influenced by crude-linked input and natural rubber price volatility
- Management expects the situation to remain stable going forward
- Weaker demand in export markets during the year, offset by a stronger domestic focus
- Moderation in feedstock prices towards the end of the year provided some relief, though margin pressure persisted due to lag effects and competitive pricing

group_structure.body: - Rishiroop Polymers Private Limited — related party: Group company from which the Company renewed a leave-and-license agreement for its Corporate Office premises at 1005, The Summit Business Bay, Andheri - Kurla Road, Andheri East, Mumbai - 400 093. The Directors' Report cites synergy of operations with other group companies as part of the justification. Transaction stated to be on arm's-length basis and not material under Section 188.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body: - **Polymers and Polymer Compounds:** Polymer blends (various grades), Complementary rubber raw materials supplied to international customers

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Non-tyre rubber goods manufacturers, largely MSMEs
- Automotive components
- Infrastructure-linked products
- General engineering applications
- Petrol hoses and LPG tubing
- O-rings, seals and gaskets
- Printing and textile rollers
- Cable sheathing
- Domestic Indian market (primary focus during the year)
- International / export markets

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Demand for the Company's products remained healthy during the year, particularly from domestic industrial segments such as automotive components, infrastructure-linked products and general engineering applications, which continue to drive rubber consumption
- The domestic rubber market was valued at approximately USD 3.3-4.2 billion in recent years and is expected to grow at a CAGR of around 5-7% over the medium term, driven by demand from automotive, infrastructure and industrial sectors
- The non-tyre segment, served largely by MSMEs, contributes over 50% of non-tyre rubber product output and is the Company's primary customer base
- Indian GDP growth estimated at approximately 6.5% in FY 2025-26, supported by strong domestic demand, sustained government capital expenditure and manufacturing momentum
- Volatility in raw material prices, including softening in petrochemical-linked inputs: while supportive of demand, it pressured realisations and margins across the polymer compounding value chain
- Stability in supply led to a fall in prices which has put margins under pressure
- The rubber industry operates in a highly competitive and price-sensitive environment due to the fragmented structure of both the user base and the supply chain, with pricing further influenced by crude-linked input and natural rubber price volatility
- Management expects the situation to remain stable going forward
- Weaker demand in export markets during the year, offset by a stronger domestic focus
- Moderation in feedstock prices towards the end of the year provided some relief, though margin pressure persisted due to lag effects and competitive pricing

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Establish a new business line in Plastics/Plastics compounding and expand capacity of the existing business at the Wadivare factory site, backed by a Board-approved estimated capex of Rs 35.00 crore
- Grow the domestic business, having mitigated weaker export-market demand through a stronger focus on domestic sales where volume growth remained encouraging
- Customise and promote new grades of polymer blends to meet the requirements of domestic and international markets
- Optimise product mix, enhance operational efficiencies and strengthen market presence while closely monitoring global developments
- Supply complementary raw materials alongside polymer blends to international customers to broaden the product portfolio and global footprint
- Continue strategic investment in Information Technology as a lever for business growth
- Continue in-house technology development for new grades of polymer blends, having brought final product quality on par with international standards (Annexure A, Technology Absorption)

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: During FY 2025-26 the Board approved estimated capital expenditure of Rs 35.00 crore for the establishment of a new business line in Plastics/Plastics compounding and for capacity expansion of the existing business, both at the Wadivare factory site. No commissioning date, ramp-up schedule or capacity quantum for this project is disclosed in the annual-report text supplied. Separately, the Company installed and commissioned an 80 KW rooftop solar system at its Nashik (Satpur) plant on September 21, 2021 (Annexure 'A' to the Directors' Report, read in the strategy_outlook bundle); capital investment on energy conservation during FY 2025-26 was stated as NIL. Capital commitments as at March 31, 2026 were NIL (previous year NIL).

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- In-house developed technologies for manufacturing various grades of polymer blends for different applications, with product quality stated to be on par with international standards (Annexure 'A', Technology Absorption — read in the strategy_outlook bundle)
- Ability to customise and promote new grades of polymer blends to meet specific domestic and international customer requirements
- Positioned as a supplier of a specialised, value-added intermediate to the fragmented non-tyre rubber segment, which accounts for over 50% of non-tyre rubber product output
- Debt-free balance sheet posture indicated by a nil Debt-Equity Ratio and nil Interest Coverage Ratio disclosed in the MD&A key-ratio table
- Product portfolio extended beyond polymer blends into complementary raw materials for international customers, broadening the global footprint

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Structural margin pressure from a highly competitive, price-sensitive rubber industry — MD&A states the industry operates in a highly competitive and price-sensitive environment because both the user base and the supply chain are fragmented, limiting the Company's ability to hold realisations.
- Raw-material and crude-linked input price volatility — MD&A notes volatility in raw material prices including petrochemical-linked inputs and natural rubber; pricing pressure is further influenced by these swings, and softening input prices depressed realisations and margins even while supporting demand.
- Realisation compression when input prices fall — Opportunities and Threats records that stability in supply caused a fall in prices which has put margins under pressure - a fall-through risk where lower input costs are passed to customers faster than they are recovered.
- Weakening global economic conditions and persistent inflation — The only risk management explicitly names in the MD&A Risks and Concerns section, flagged as a potential area of concern.
- Export-market demand weakness and geopolitical / trade disruption — The Directors' Report describes heightened geopolitical tensions, regional conflicts, tariff realignments and supply chain diversification creating uncertainty in global growth; the Company saw weaker demand in export markets during the year and had to lean on domestic sales to offset it.
- Single-segment concentration in Polymers and Polymer Compounds — MD&A states the primary segment the Company operates in is Polymers and Polymer Compounds and their related products, so there is no diversification cushion against a downturn in rubber compounding; the planned Plastics compounding line is the stated response.
- Earnings sensitivity to a quoted investment portfolio held outside the operating business — MD&A and the Directors' Report attribute the fall in other income and the reduction in Return on Networth to a sharp fall in the value of the investment portfolio and to fair valuation of quoted investments decreasing amid subdued financial markets - non-operating earnings that swing with equity markets.
- Very small operating scale and thin management bench — MD&A discloses the Company currently employs about 35 employees in all categories, a small base relative to the newly approved Plastics/Plastics compounding business line and Wadivare capacity expansion it must execute.
